title: 6-color conjecture for cubic bipartite planar graph squares
statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic bipartite planar graph, and let $G^2$ be its square, obtained by joining vertices at distance at most $2$ in $G$. Let $\chi(G^2)$ denote the chromatic number of $G^2$.

**Cubic bipartite planar square-coloring conjecture.** The square satisfies

$$
\chi(G^2)\leq 6.
$$

This is a strengthening of the general cubic planar bound in Wegner's conjecture and is presented as an open problem for cubic bipartite planar graphs.
source_name: Seog-Jin Kim and Rong Luo, “Squares of subcubic planar graphs without cycles of length 4-8 are 6-choosable”, arXiv:2512.10175 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10175

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2025). “The case $\Delta(G)=3$ was confirmed by Thomassen and independently by Hartke, Jahanbekam, and Thomas using extensive computer-assisted case analysis.”
